item.title: Flying Fijians to face South Africa ahead of World Cup next year
item.description: A new chapter for the FIJI Water Flying Fijians will unfold on Australia’s Central Coast next year, with Fiji set to face the four-time world champion Springboks in a Test match ahead of the 2027 Rugby World Cup. The Flying Fijians will face South Africa at Polytec Stadium on Saturday, September 18th next year, in a match dubbed the ‘Contest on the Coast’.
item.content:encoded:
A new chapter for the FIJI Water Flying Fijians will unfold on Australia’s Central Coast next year, with Fiji set to face the four-time world champion Springboks in a Test match ahead of the 2027 Rugby World Cup.

The Flying Fijians will face South Africa at Polytec Stadium on Saturday, September 18th next year, in a match dubbed the ‘Contest on the Coast’.

The Test will be only the fourth meeting between Fiji and South Africa and will form part of both teams’ final preparations for the 2027 Rugby World Cup.

The Fiji Rugby Union says the match was officially launched today, exactly one year before kick-off, marking the return of international rugby to the Central Coast for the first time since 2004.

FRU says South Africa last played on the Central Coast in 2004 when the Springboks faced a combined Pacific Islands team.

FRU Chief Executive Officer Koli Sewabu says they are delighted to confirm the historic Test against one of the most respected and successful teams in world rugby.

Sewabu says the Springboks have set the benchmark in world rugby and Fiji’s players relish every opportunity to test themselves against the best.

He says the fixture is about more than a rugby match, as it will provide an opportunity to inspire Fijians, engage the global Fijian community and showcase Fiji’s style, spirit and talent.

Sewabu says Fiji Rugby is grateful to its partners for helping bring the event to life and providing a platform to celebrate international rugby and strengthen the connection between the two rugby nations.

He says the match will also provide valuable high-performance preparation as the Flying Fijians continue to build towards the 2027 Rugby World Cup and their long-term objectives.

Sewabu says Fiji Rugby is looking forward to seeing the strong Fijian community across Australia turn out in force to support the Flying Fijians in Gosford.

Springboks Head Coach Rassie Erasmus says the team is excited about the fixture and the opportunity to play another Test on the Central Coast.

Erasmus says Fiji are a quality team that have consistently tested some of the top teams in the world over the last few years.

He says Fiji’s quarter-final appearance at the 2023 Rugby World Cup proved the Flying Fijians can be a force to be reckoned with.

Erasmus says Fiji are among the top 10 ranked teams in the world and are a physical and talented side.

He says the match will provide both teams with an important test before the 2027 Rugby World Cup begins.

The 2027 Rugby World Cup will be staged across Australia, giving the Flying Fijians an opportunity to play in front of supporters in the region during their final preparations.

The visit will extend beyond the Test match, with both teams expected to establish training camps and participate in community activities aimed at increasing local engagement and generating economic benefits for the region .

Central Coast Mayor Lawrie McKinna says the Test will showcase the region to visitors from across Australia and around the world.

McKinna says the event is expected to bring people into local hotels, restaurants, cafes and businesses while delivering economic benefits to the region.

He says with only 20,000 seats available, fans are encouraged to secure their tickets early.

McKinna says the match will also give local residents, young players and sporting clubs the opportunity to connect with some of the biggest names in world rugby.

The Test match has been secured through an investment package from the Central Coast Council.

Tickets will go on public sale at 10am on Tuesday, 29 September 2026 through Ticketek.

The clash will give Australian fans an opportunity to see the Flying Fijians and Springboks in action before the 2027 Rugby World Cup.

item.title: Okeanos Explorer makes first Fiji visit to map Pacific’s deep seafloor
item.description: The U.S. deep-sea exploration vessel Okeanos Explorer is in Fiji for the first time, carrying out scientific exploration and seafloor mapping to improve understanding of the Pacific’s largely unexplored deep waters. The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration’s (NOAA) Okeanos Explorer docked in Suva yesterday as part of its 2026 Pacific exploration operations.
item.content:encoded:
The U.S. deep-sea exploration vessel Okeanos Explorer is in Fiji for the first time, carrying out scientific exploration and seafloor mapping to improve understanding of the Pacific’s largely unexplored deep waters.

The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration’s (NOAA) Okeanos Explorer docked in Suva yesterday as part of its 2026 Pacific exploration operations.

The vessel is expected to remain in Fiji for about three more days before departing for American Samoa, where it will carry out further deep-sea mapping.

NOAA Expedition Coordinator Nikki Morgan says the team’s work involves identifying areas of scientific interest, securing the necessary permits and planning sites where the vessel’s remotely operated vehicle can be deployed.

The Okeanos Explorer is equipped with four types of mapping sonars and a remotely operated vehicle capable of diving to depths of 6,000 metres.

Morgan says the vessel collects mapping data, video, imagery and other information to help build knowledge of areas of the ocean that remain poorly understood.

She says the raw and processed data collected in Fiji waters, including geo-referenced imagery, will be made available to the Fijian Government, while the final data will also be publicly accessible.

Morgan says the data being collected in Fiji does not contain information on mineral resources, as the focus of the current work is on documenting what the seafloor looks like.

She says NOAA does not restrict the data to particular users, with information made available for commercial, public and research purposes.

The aim, she says, is to reduce what is unknown about the seafloor and provide information that can assist researchers, governments and policymakers in making decisions.

The U.S. Embassy in Suva hosted Fiji media personnel on board the vessel to learn more about its scientific exploration and seafloor mapping work.

Chargé d’Affaires Christina Cavallo says the United States supports transparency in ocean scientific research and the sharing of information to help Pacific partners make informed decisions about managing their resources.

NOAA Ocean Exploration plans to spend more than 150 days at sea aboard the Okeanos Explorer this year, exploring deep waters around Hawai‘i, the Cook Islands, American Samoa and Fiji.

After its work in American Samoa, the vessel will head to Honolulu for its winter maintenance.
